cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Approach above the red hub using current camera geometry; level the hand and keep fingers open.
Descend toward hub grasp height while correcting the remaining small hand tilt.
Center the fingers on the red hub, finish the approach, and close to the demonstrated hub-grasp width.
Lift vertically with the hub held; check that the red gear rises with the hand before transferring.
Carry the visibly retained red gear above the vacant spindle, allowing for its small offset within the fingers.
Lower the centered gear toward the spindle in small vertical increments; maintain hub retention.
Continue a slow vertical insertion to the expected seated height, watching for lateral displacement.
The gear appears to have stopped above its seat. Lift clear and correct alignment toward the spindle inferred from the paired gear.
Reapproach the spindle with the corrected fore-aft alignment and a small lateral adjustment.
Back off from the apparent rim contact and refine spindle alignment between the previous two approaches.
Align the hub over the visible post and approach its top; the exact seating depth is still uncertain.
Lower to seating height with a small yaw adjustment to help the teeth engage.
The gear remains perched above the seat. Lift and move aside to expose the spindle for a fresh visual alignment.
Return above the newly exposed spindle with an intermediate alignment and clearance for a gentle insertion.
Lower the aligned red gear and gently yaw during the final approach to mesh the teeth.
Corrected tensor after zero execution. Search a few millimeters across the spindle with gentle yaw.
Sweep gently back across the spindle at fixed height while allowing tooth alignment.
Bring the hub leftward over the spindle projection with a small counter-yaw; avoid further downward pressure while alignment is uncertain.
Relax the grasp over the spindle to let the gear settle, then lift the fingers slightly to inspect its seating.
Regrasp the perched hub, correct a few millimeters toward the post center, and test a short descent.
Continue the short descent while rotating gently to clear tooth-on-tooth interference.
Test engagement by rotating the held gear about the post, with only a small additional seating motion.
Continue the in-place drive rotation and check whether the paired gear responds.
The hub still appears high. Lift off the rim and correct toward the spindle using its exposed top rather than the paired gear.
Lower from the corrected alignment while gently turning to engage the gear teeth.
Apply a controlled drive rotation at the lowered position and observe whether the paired gear turns.
Continue rotating at fixed height now that the red gear appears aligned with the base; check engagement without pressing farther down.
The hub still seems perched. Lift and expose the post again for a precise alignment check rather than continuing unsupported rotation.
The base lifted with the gear. Return it to the table and release gently so the assembly can settle before attempting another supported turn.
Clear the fingers from the released assembly and let it settle so the post and gear alignment can be inspected.
Approach the tilted red hub at its new location with open fingers, preparing to lift it clear for an unobstructed post alignment.
Close around the red hub and lift gently, checking whether only the gear is retained or the base remains attached.
The previous lift did not retain the gear. Open and approach lower around the exposed hub before closing again.
Close at the lower hub height and perform a short vertical retention test.
Lift the retained gear clear and shift aside to expose the actual spindle position.
Open and pause clear of the shifted assembly so it can settle onto the tabletop.
Approach the red hub at its settled location, keeping the fingers open for a centered regrasp.
Center on the hub seen in the wrist view, descend a short distance, and close around it without lifting the base.
Gently seat and turn the centered red hub while leaving the base supported on the table.
Continue the supported drive turn with a small seating descent; monitor whether the red gear settles rather than carrying the base.
